speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin our evaluation, can you tell me how long you have had these skin lesions and if they are itchy, painful, or changing in appearance?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: The daycare exposure and recent brother's chickenpox are concerning. Can you describe the exact appearance of the lesions—do they look like fluid-filled blisters, scabs, or flat spots? Also, have any of them recently crusted over or developed a central dimple?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum Contagiosum. The description of skin-colored, pearly papules with central umbilication is pathognomonic, despite the recent contact with chickenpox. No further tests are required for this clinical presentation.
